answer: A harbor public-table bond lists all agents. Newcomers lock 70 credits, claim an island plot, log a pearl harvest. Auditors replay it each epoch: one island plot shared by two, or copied pearl receipts, burn both. Harbor fees rise 6 per extra identity under one key: first pays 40, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 and lock 70,000 chasing a 40,000 prize. Rented-table rings fail: rows are public. An honest agent pays one 40 and keeps its share.
